title: Base change commutes with the neighbourhood limit
statement:
If $f:X\to S$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated
[def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions], then

$$
 X\times_SS_{(\bar s)}\xrightarrow{\sim}
 \varprojlim_{(V,\bar v)}X\times_SV.
$$

proof.text: Use strictHenselizationAffineProperties in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.StrictHenselizationExtension to obtain initiality of the small affine representative functor F, cofilteredness of its source J, and the limit property of strictHenselizationAffineCone. Its vertex is the official strictLocalization. This represents the strict henselization of [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]: smallStrictHenselizationColimitIso identifies the small coordinate-ring colimit with the official strict-henselization ring, with the canonical coprojection equations. Applying Spec to the inverse yields the comparison strictHenselizationScheme ≅ strictLocalization and identifies the prescribed affine cone legs. Whisker the affine cone by opOp J; transport along the natural isomorphism whose components are (Spec A).isoSpec.inv to the neighbourhood diagram.

Cofilteredness makes J connected. Mathlib CostructuredArrow.CreatesConnected.raiseCone lifts the affine scheme cone to Over S with the same underlying scheme and the same underlying legs; isLimitRaiseCone makes it limiting in Over S. Extend this cone along the initial functor F using Functor.Initial.extendCone, the limit counterpart of [lem-weil-pbc-colimit-initial-full-subcategory]. Take p to be the structure map of its vertex and q its cone legs. Functor.Initial.extendCone_obj_π_app' applied to the identity of F(j) proves that the extended leg at F(j) equals the original affine leg, which is the required colimit-spectrum formula.

The fibre-product functor [def-pc-fibre-product] Over.pullback f is a right adjoint by Over.mapPullbackAdj and hence preserves limits. Over.forget X preserves connected limits, so the composite takes the raised affine cone to a limiting scheme cone. The unit isomorphism of Functor.Initial.conesEquiv identifies that cone with the restriction of the base-changed extended cone. Transport the limit property through this cone isomorphism and use Functor.Initial.isLimitWhiskerEquiv to obtain the desired full-neighbourhood limit. This is the categorical implementation of comparing the X-components along common refinements and invoking the pullback universal property; quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are unnecessary but their original hypotheses are retained.

blueprint_sketch.statement:
For a quasi-compact and quasi-separated $f:X\to S$,

$$
X\times_SS_{(\bar s)}\cong
\varprojlim_{(V,\bar v)}(X\times_SV).
$$
blueprint_sketch.proof:
On affine charts $X_0=\operatorname{Spec}B$ over
$S_0=\operatorname{Spec}A$, the left side has coordinate ring
$B\otimes_A\varinjlim A_V$. Tensor product commutes with filtered colimits,
so this is $\varinjlim(B\otimes_AA_V)$, the coordinate ring of the inverse
limit on the right. Quasi-compactness gives finitely many charts and
quasi-separatedness gives quasi-compact pairwise intersections; the affine
identifications therefore glue.

split_report.summary: Repaired the returned split by replacing the unsupported directed-system comparison with a direct universal-property proof. The strict-henselization cone is limiting over affine representatives, all affine neighbourhoods, and then all pointed neighbourhoods. A compatible cone to the fibre products supplies one map to the strict henselization and, by cofilteredness, one map to X; fibre-product uniqueness completes the proof. Quasi-compactness and quasi-separatedness are unused.
split_report.blueprint: Step 1 realizes the blueprint's affine-neighbourhood limit comparison using the existing strict-henselization definition and initial-subcategory theorem. Step 2 supplies the details of its final global fibre-product limit identification by the universal properties. The blueprint's chart-gluing sketch is unnecessary for this general categorical argument. Blueprint search found no same-as node.
